svg.text: Scaling strategy: frontend delivery, backend services, storage, search, deployment
Static assets, image resizing, edge caching
SSG/ISR for listing pages, client-side data for personalized state
Horizontal scaling per service based on load; rolling deploys, blue/green releases
Kubernetes / ECS, health checks, circuit breakers between services
Metrics dashboards, alerting on error rate / latency SLOs
Listing pages pre-rendered (SSG/ISR) and served from the CDN edge — most traffic
never reaches origin. Personalized data is fetched client-side.
Denormalized listing index in OpenSearch, updated async via the message
broker on listing/price/availability changes — keeps writes off the read path.
Stateless services behind the gateway scale horizontally and independently —
a booking traffic spike doesn't require scaling search, and vice versa.
Canary releases per service with automated rollback on error-rate/latency
regression; blue/green for the frontend to avoid asset/version mismatches.
Read-heavy listing data offloaded to Redis and read replicas. Booking writes
stay on a smaller, strongly-consistent primary to avoid double-booking.
Circuit breakers between services; payment/booking failures degrade
gracefully rather than cascading into search/browse traffic.
Booking Service — it's the only strongly-consistent write path (no double-booking), so it scales
via read replicas + row-level locking on availability, not just adding more stateless instances.
